## Summary

- **Why:** the protein language model (pLM) benchmark panel is now *Mnemiopsis*, oyster, *Ciona* and zebrafish (urchin dropped). Two well-annotated reference species, **human** and ***Drosophila***, are being added as immune datasets.
- **Fly:** circulating hemocytes from healthy, not-infested late-L3 larvae (Cattenoz et al. 2020, 10x 3'). **7,517 cells**, author cluster labels.
- **Human:** the CellTypist cross-tissue immune atlas (Domínguez Conde et al. 2022), **10x 3' v3 donors only**, myeloid compartment plus mast cells, T/B/NK cells, and (revised the same day) progenitors and erythroid cells, so that every zebrafish cell type in the earlier SATURN run has a human counterpart. **10,541 cells** in the first build; the revised build adds 1,000 progenitors and 78 erythroid cells, for **11,619 cells** (job 599517).
- **Proteomes:** Ensembl release 113 for both (same release as zebrafish). Links in [Proteomes](#proteomes) (also what Ingrid needs for ESMC).
- **Status:** SATURN inputs built; ESM-1b embeddings running on Pegasus (jobs 599440 Dmel, 599441 Hsap). The human h5ad will be rebuilt with the revised composition; the embeddings are unaffected because the gene list does not change.
- **Update 2026-10-16 (QC, `07f`):** both inputs are clean and the author labels match canonical markers; no cells removed. Human is ~3× deeper than the other species, and donor is confounded with cell type for several human groups. Three decisions open (human label granularity, human depth, small fly groups). See [Section 5](#qc-update).
:::

# Key terms

| Term | Meaning here |
|---|---|
| **Hemocytes / plasmatocytes** | Fly blood cells. Plasmatocytes are the phagocytic, macrophage-like majority; crystal cells (CC) and lamellocytes (LM) are minor types. |
| **L3 / wandering L3** | Third (last) larval stage; "wandering" larvae have left the food, shortly before pupation. |
| **10x 3' v3 / 5' v1–v2** | 10x Chromium library chemistries. 3' and 5' kits capture different ends of each transcript, so they are not mixed within a species here. |
| **`raw.X`** | Where CELLxGENE h5ad files keep the raw integer counts (`X` holds normalised values). |
| **Isoform** | One protein product of a gene. Ensembl `pep.all` lists every isoform; SATURN combines isoform embeddings into one gene embedding. |

: Terms used in this entry. {#tbl-terms}

# 1. Datasets used

| Species | Dataset | What | Chemistry | Accession |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| *Drosophila melanogaster* (Dmel) | Cattenoz et al. 2020, *EMBO J* | circulating hemocytes, not-infested (NI) wandering L3 larvae, OregonR, pool of 20 females | 10x 3' | ArrayExpress [E-MTAB-8698](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/biostudies/arrayexpress/studies/E-MTAB-8698) (library RRCZ22; Cell Ranger matrices + author labels `NI_cell_cluster_ID.txt`) |
| *Homo sapiens* (Hsap) | Domínguez Conde et al. 2022, *Science* (CellTypist) | immune cells isolated from 16 tissues of organ donors; myeloid compartment + global object | 10x 3' v3 subset (also 5' v1/v2 in the full atlas) | CELLxGENE collection [62ef75e4](https://cellxgene.cziscience.com/collections/62ef75e4-cbea-454e-a0ce-998ec40223d3): Myeloid compartment (51,552 cells), Global (329,762 cells) |

: Datasets used for the two new species. {#tbl-datasets}

**Why these.** Both are whole-cell 10x data from healthy animals or donors, matching the other species. Cattenoz uses late (wandering) L3 larvae: in a cross-species comparison, late-larval plasmatocytes were the hemocytes most similar to vertebrate macrophages (Yoon et al. 2023), which gives SATURN an expected answer to check. CellTypist covers tissue-resident macrophages (lung, gut, spleen), not just blood monocytes, with expert-curated labels.

# 2. Download and inspection (`07b`, `07c`)

`07b` downloads both datasets on the `transfers` queue (md5 checks pass for both Cattenoz archives). `07c` is a read-only diagnostic.

**Fly.** 7,606 cells × 13,926 genes, all FlyBase `FBgn` IDs, integer counts. Median 2,930 UMIs, 959 genes and 4.9% mitochondrial reads per cell. 7,517 barcodes have an author label; the 89 unlabelled cells have a median of only 352 genes (vs 961) and were dropped as low-quality.

**Human.** Raw integer counts are in `raw.X` for both files, and labels agree 100% between the Myeloid and Global objects. **Only 2 of the 12 donors (D496, D503) were sequenced with 3' v3**; the other 10 are 5'. Restricting to 3' v3 leaves 34,863 myeloid cells, dominated by classical monocytes (16,047) and alveolar macrophages (13,869, almost all lung). Smaller macrophage types: intestinal 484, intermediate 321, erythrophagocytic 77. No liver (Kupffer) cells and no neutrophils on 3' v3. Mast cells (3,110) are in the Global object, not the Myeloid one.

# 3. Building the SATURN inputs (`07d`)

Same format as `01_prepare_h5ads.sh`: raw counts in `X` (CSR), `obs['cell_type']` and `obs['species']`, written to `02_processed_h5ad/{Dmel,Hsap}_saturn.h5ad`. Cell names are prefixed `Dmel_` / `Hsap_` so barcodes cannot collide across species. Extra `obs` columns (`tissue`, `donor_id`, `sample_group`) are kept for interpretation; SATURN reads only `cell_type`.

- **Fly:** the 7,517 labelled cells; `cell_type` = author cluster.
- **Human:** `cell_type` = `Manually_curated_celltype`; subsampled (seed 42) so the rare macrophage types are not swamped:
  - kept in full: nonclassical monocytes, intestinal / intermediate / erythrophagocytic macrophages, DC1, DC2, migDC, cycling;
  - classical monocytes: 600 each from blood, spleen, bone marrow and lung;
  - alveolar macrophages: 2,400;
  - mast cells: 500, the only granule-storing (granulocyte-like) human cells available, as a comparison for granular invertebrate cells (e.g. the eosinophil-like Mlei_16). Treated as supporting evidence only;
  - lymphocyte slice: ~286 each of CD4 T, CD8 T, γδ T, MAIT, NK, B and plasma cells, as counterparts of the zebrafish T and B cells (first planned as a negative control);
  - **added in the revision:** all 3' v3 progenitors and erythroid cells, each capped at 1,000 (counterparts of zebrafish HPC / myeloid progenitors and erythroid cells);
  - dropped: doublets, megakaryocytes and other minor lymphoid states.

**Why mirror the zebrafish cell types (revision).** In the earlier zebrafish / *Ciona* / *Mnemiopsis* SATURN run, the zebrafish input included macrophages, neutrophils, eosinophils, HPC, myeloid progenitors, T cells, B cells and erythroid cells. Zebrafish and human are the closest pair in the panel, so each zebrafish type should have a human counterpart to land with; if they do not co-cluster, the more distant matches cannot be trusted. Erythroid cells also serve as a check: in that run, zebrafish erythroid cells merged with a *Ciona* progenitor-like population (cLRP-1), which cannot be a homologous cell type. The new cells are sampled after all earlier picks (same seed), so the original 10,541 cells are unchanged. Remaining gap: no human neutrophils or eosinophils on 3' v3 (mast cells are the nearest granulocyte-like cells), and only 78 erythroid cells.

| Species | Group | Cell types (n cells) | Total |

# 4. Proteomes and embeddings (`07e`, `02_embed.sh`) {#proteomes}

Ensembl release 113 for both species, the same release as the zebrafish proteome:

| Species | Protein FASTA (Ensembl 113) | GTF | Proteins / genes | Pegasus copy |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hsap | [Homo_sapiens.GRCh38.pep.all.fa.gz](https://ftp.ensembl.org/pub/release-113/fasta/homo_sapiens/pep/Homo_sapiens.GRCh38.pep.all.fa.gz) | [Homo_sapiens.GRCh38.113.gtf.gz](https://ftp.ensembl.org/pub/release-113/gtf/homo_sapiens/Homo_sapiens.GRCh38.113.gtf.gz) | 123,845 / 23,864 | `/scratch/dark_genes/SATURN_Mnemi/01_proteomes/Hsap/` |
| Dmel | [Drosophila_melanogaster.BDGP6.46.pep.all.fa.gz](https://ftp.ensembl.org/pub/release-113/fasta/drosophila_melanogaster/pep/Drosophila_melanogaster.BDGP6.46.pep.all.fa.gz) | [Drosophila_melanogaster.BDGP6.46.113.gtf.gz](https://ftp.ensembl.org/pub/release-113/gtf/drosophila_melanogaster/Drosophila_melanogaster.BDGP6.46.113.gtf.gz) | 30,799 / 13,986 | `/scratch/dark_genes/SATURN_Mnemi/01_proteomes/Dmel/` |

: Proteomes for the two new species. {#tbl-proteomes}

**Gene → protein mapping.** The h5ad gene IDs are Ensembl IDs (`ENSG…`, `FBgn…`), so a new `ensembl_gene_id` strategy in `02_embed.sh` reads the `gene:` field of each protein header (version suffix stripped) and maps each gene to **all** of its isoforms, the same as zebrafish. Only proteins of genes present in the h5ad are embedded; these are written to `03_embeddings/{Dmel,Hsap}/{SP}_filtered.faa`, which is the exact protein set to use for any other model.

::: {.callout-note}
## For Ingrid (ESMC-600M)

The filtered FASTAs (`/scratch/dark_genes/SATURN_Mnemi/03_embeddings/Dmel/Dmel_filtered.faa` and `.../Hsap/Hsap_filtered.faa`, written by step 1 of `02_embed.sh`) contain exactly the proteins embedded with ESM-1b. If those are not convenient, the full Ensembl 113 `pep.all` files above work too: the gene ID is in the `gene:` field of each header.
:::

ESM-1b settings are unchanged (`esm1b_t33_650M_UR50S`, layer 33, mean pooling, truncation 1,022). Both jobs run on the `normal` queue with 8 cores on one host and 4 GB per core.

# 5. Update 2026-10-16: QC and per-species UMAPs (`07f`) {#qc-update}

While the embeddings run, `07f_QC_UMAP_Dmel_Hsap.sh` checks the quality of the two SATURN inputs and draws a UMAP for each species with the author labels. It only reads the `*_saturn.h5ad` files and changes nothing in them. Each species is processed on its own, with no integration and no filtering: normalise to 10,000 counts, log1p, 2,000 highly variable genes (`seurat_v3`), 50 PCs, 15 neighbours on 30 PCs, UMAP, and Leiden clusters at resolution 1.0 for reference only. Cells are **flagged, not removed**, if they lie more than 5 median absolute deviations (MADs) from the median on log UMI count or log gene count, or if their mitochondrial share is more than 3 MADs above the median.

**Result: both datasets are clean, and the author labels agree with canonical markers in both species. No cells need removing.**

| Species | Cells | Labels | Median UMIs | Median genes | Median % mito | Flagged |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mlei | 10,239 | 20 | 2,239 | 860 | – | – |
| Cgig | 37,668 | 13 | 1,947 | 757 | – | – |
| Crob | 15,575 | 33 | 6,138 | 1,494 | – | – |
| Drer | 6,532 | 9 | 3,141 | 872 | – | – |
| **Dmel** | 7,517 | 16 | 2,942 | 961 | 4.9 | 550 (7.3%) |
| **Hsap** | 11,619 | 31 | 9,604 | 2,657 | 7.4 | 962 (8.3%) |

## Fly

- **Quality is tight:** mito reads are about 5% with no low-quality tail, as expected after the authors' 500-gene cutoff. Ribosomal reads are about 37%, normal for fly.
- **Markers match the labels** (@fig-dmel-dot): crystal cells (CC) express *PPO1*, *PPO2* and *lz*; lamellocytes *atilla*, *Itgbn* and *mys*; PL-prolif *stg* and *polo*; PL-Lsp *Lsp2*; PL-Rel *Rel*; PL-Inos *Inos*; plasmatocytes *NimC1*, *eater*, *Pxn* and *crq*.
- **Flags reflect biology:** 40% of crystal cells are flagged, but only because they carry more UMIs (median 7,887). They are kept.
- **Very small groups:** lamellocytes are only 8 cells (LM-1 6, LM-2 2), as expected in uninfected larvae. **PL-ImpL2** (21 cells) sits far from all other cells on the UMAP, has low depth (median 1,373 UMIs) and weak *srp*, *Hml* and *NimC1*; it may not be hemocytes and should be checked before it is treated as a plasmatocyte subtype.
- **The main plasmatocyte groups grade into one another:** PL-0, PL-1 and PL-2 form a continuum and are split across several Leiden clusters, consistent with the original paper.

![Fly hemocytes (Cattenoz NI), coloured by author cluster.](/images/20261016_Dmel_umap_celltype_ondata.png){#fig-dmel-umap}

![Canonical fly hemocyte markers by author cluster (colour scaled per gene).](/images/20261016_Dmel_dotplot_markers_by_celltype.png){#fig-dmel-dot}

![Fly QC by author cluster: log10 UMIs, genes, % mitochondrial and % ribosomal reads (medians marked).](/images/20261016_Dmel_violin_qc_by_celltype.png){#fig-dmel-qc}

## Human

- **Markers match the labels** (@fig-hsap-dot): *CLEC9A*/*XCR1* in DC1, *CD1C*/*FCER1A* in DC2, *CCR7*/*LAMP3* in migDC, *MARCO*/*FABP4* in alveolar macrophages, *KIT*/*TPSAB1*/*CPA3* in mast cells, *CD34*/*PRSS57* in progenitors, and the expected T, NK and B cell markers.
- **Mito flags follow tissue:** all 962 flagged cells are above the 14.2% mito cutoff (none on depth), and intestinal macrophages have the highest share (22.7%), consistent with gut dissociation. The atlas was already filtered by its authors, so all cells are kept.
- **Erythroid cells look like progenitors:** the 78 erythroid cells express *MKI67*, *TOP2A* and *PRSS57* and cluster with the progenitors (one Leiden cluster holds 202 progenitors and 78 erythroid cells), so they are erythroid progenitors rather than mature red cells. Keep this in mind if the zebrafish erythroid cells are mature.
- **Donor and cell type are tied together:** 96% of alveolar macrophages come from D496, while progenitors (94%), nonclassical monocytes (93%) and DCs come mostly from D503. This reflects which tissues each donor gave, so donor effects cannot be separated from cell type for these groups. Classical monocytes, sampled evenly across four tissues, are the only well-mixed group (@fig-hsap-meta). No correction is planned, but it is listed in the caveats.

![Human CellTypist 3' v3 subset, coloured by curated cell type.](/images/20261016_Hsap_umap_celltype_ondata.png){#fig-hsap-umap}

![Canonical human immune markers by curated cell type (colour scaled per gene).](/images/20261016_Hsap_dotplot_markers_by_celltype.png){#fig-hsap-dot}

![Human UMAP coloured by QC flag, Leiden cluster, tissue, donor and sampling group.](/images/20261016_Hsap_umap_meta.png){#fig-hsap-meta}

## Open decisions

1. **Human label granularity.** SATURN uses each species' labels to guide training. Human now has 31 fine labels, against 16 for fly and 9 for zebrafish. Options: keep them; collapse the 18 lymphocyte subtypes to the 7 groups in `sample_group` (CD4 T, CD8 T, γδ T, MAIT, NK, B, plasma); or use Leiden clusters, as for the other species.
2. **Human depth.** Downsample human counts towards the depth of the other species, or leave them. This matters for a benchmark, but it would be a new step and needs agreeing first.
3. **Small fly groups.** Keep LM-1/LM-2 (perhaps merged as "LM") and PL-ImpL2 as they are, or merge or drop them.

Outputs: `/scratch/dark_genes/SATURN_Mnemi/07_new_species_QC/20261016_Dmel_Hsap_QC/` on Pegasus (`summary.txt`, per-cell-type QC tables, per-cell UMAP + QC CSVs, figures), synced locally to `output/SATURN/20261016_Dmel_Hsap_QC/` without the h5ad files.

# 6. Troubleshooting on Pegasus

- **Batch jobs don't read `~/.bashrc`.** `source ~/.bashrc; conda activate` made the inspection job exit in 0.1 s with empty logs. Fix: `source ~/anaconda3/bin/activate` then `conda activate saturn_protein`, wrapped in `set +u` / `set -u` (conda's scripts reference unset variables). `02_embed.sh` now has the same wrapper.
- **`grep -q` + `pipefail`.** `conda env list | grep -q saturn_protein` can return false even when the env exists (grep closes the pipe early). Test for the env folder instead.
- **Bigmem affinity error.** `-n 4 -R "rusage[mem=96000]"` pended with "not enough processor units to satisfy the job affinity request". Memory appears to be charged per core (4 × 96 GB). Fix: request total memory ÷ cores and add `span[hosts=1]`; light jobs go to `normal`.
- **Empty `.out` files.** With `#BSUB -N`, the LSF job summary (exit code, reason) is emailed instead of written to the `.out` file; use `bjobs -a -l <id>` or `bhist -l <id>`.
- **Ensembl blocks recursive `wget`.** `ftp.ensembl.org/robots.txt` is `Disallow: /`, so `wget -r -A <pattern>` downloads only the directory listing and exits "successfully". Fix: explicit file URLs, and a check that each FASTA is non-empty. (The older `07a` used the recursive pattern too.)

# Caveats

- **Human = 2 donors**, about 52% / 48% of cells; donor and tissue effects cannot be separated from each other within human. The QC update shows donor is also tied to cell type: alveolar macrophages are 96% D496, progenitors and nonclassical monocytes ~93% D503.
- **Human depth:** median 9,604 UMIs per cell, against 1,947–6,138 for the other five species (@tbl-qc-xsp).
- **Fly = one library, one strain** (OregonR, pooled females). The Yoon et al. 2023 w1118 10x data (GEO GSE184781, ~2.2k cells, with labels) is a possible robustness check.
- **No human neutrophils**; mast cells are the only granulocyte-like human cells, and a mapping to them should be read as "granular secretory cell", not "eosinophil".
- **Considered, not used: a dedicated human bone marrow dataset** (HCA immune census, 8 donors), which would better match the zebrafish input (kidney marrow cell types: HPC, myeloid progenitors, erythroid, neutrophils, eosinophils). Not used because it is older 10x chemistry, the released matrices have no cell calling or expert labels, and 10x bone marrow data generally contain few or no neutrophils and eosinophils (low RNA content; density separation), so it would not fill the granulocyte gap. A sorted neutrophil dataset (Montaldo et al. 2022, 10x 3' v3, FASTQ only) remains the option if granulocytes become important.
- **Check the zebrafish source.** Project notes cite Jiao et al. (GSE186158), but that study profiled spleen with 10x v2, whereas the zebrafish input has kidney-marrow cell types and non-10x, `_Dr_kidney` barcodes.
- **Progenitor and erythroid matches may reflect cell state** (proliferation, ribosomal/translation programs) rather than homology; check the macrogenes driving any cluster they join before interpreting it.
- **Methods wording:** the methods draft says "the longest protein isoform per gene was embedded", but `02_embed.sh` maps genes to all isoforms (zebrafish, and now fly and human). Check the other species and correct the text.
